Listen to this article Share Food is fundamental to human life, health, dignity, and economic progress. Beyond meeting a basic need, a reliable supply of safe, nutritious, and affordable food supports families, sustains livelihoods, and helps communities and economies thrive. Ensuring that food is available to people consistently therefore requires more than growing crops; it calls for resilient systems that can process, distribute, and deliver food efficiently. At BUA Foods, we understand the responsibility that comes with being part of this essential sector. Our work extends beyond manufacturing and selling food products. We are committed to strengthening domestic food production, deepening local value chains, and building the industrial capacity needed to serve a growing population while contributing to Nigeria’s economic development. These priorities give particular relevance to this year’s World Food Day theme, “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow.” It is a timely reminder that the food systems we build today will determine our ability to nourish future generations sustainably, affordably, and reliably. For countries such as Nigeria, this conversation has never been more important. Innovation is not merely about technology or scientific breakthroughs. It is about finding smarter and more efficient ways to produce, process, distribute, and make food accessible at scale. More importantly, it is about ensuring that these solutions reach the millions of people who depend on them every day. This is where the future of food security must be anchored. Food security requires more than agriculture Nigeria and Africa possess immense agricultural potential. However, agricultural production alone cannot guarantee food security. Food security requires a complete ecosystem: the ability to process what is produced, move it efficiently across markets, preserve quality, reduce waste, and ensure affordability for consumers. It requires infrastructure, supply chains, manufacturing capacity, and investment. This is why I firmly believe that the future of Africa’s food security will be determined not only on farms but also in factories. At BUA Foods, we recognise that our role extends far beyond manufacturing and selling food products. We see ourselves as part of a broader national effort to strengthen domestic food production, deepen local value chains, and build the industrial capacity required to support a rapidly growing population. Our journey reflects this commitment. When BUA Foods was listed on the Nigerian Exchange, we were considerably smaller than some of the established players in the industry. Through disciplined execution, prudent capital allocation, operational excellence, and a relentless focus on long-term value creation, we steadily strengthened our position. Today, that journey has brought us to an entirely different level of scale and capability. Building Scale for National Impact In 2025, BUA Foods recorded revenue of ₦1.77 trillion, representing 16% growth, while profit after tax increased by 95% to ₦518.4 billion. Total assets also grew by 27% to ₦1.39 trillion. While these numbers are significant, they are not the true story. The more important story is what this scale enables us to do. We are expanding our wheat milling operations, completing investments in our edible oils business, strengthening existing manufacturing facilities, and introducing new product categories, including noodles. Collectively, these investments are expected to increase production capacity across the business by more than 50%, with some divisions achieving capacity growth of up to 100% as new projects come on stream. This is industrialisation with purpose. The recent introduction of BUA Foods Bakers Pride Flour is another practical expression of this commitment. Launched in Kano, the product was developed with the realities of everyday Nigerian bakers in mind. Its proposition is built around smart choice, dependable baking, and more possibilities, with versatility for different baking needs, from conventional bread loaves to other baked products. The ambition is straightforward: to offer bakers a relevant flour choice that supports consistent quality, reliable performance, and confidence in every bake. Every additional tonne of food produced locally strengthens national supply capacity. Every new production line stimulates economic activity across suppliers, transporters, distributors, retailers, and countless small businesses. Every investment in manufacturing capability reinforces the resilience of our food system and reduces our dependence on external supply shocks. When industrial growth is aligned with national priorities, its impact extends far beyond company performance. It becomes a catalyst for economic stability, food availability, and shared prosperity. Innovation must ultimately improve lives Innovation, however, should never become an end in itself. Its true value lies in its ability to improve lives. As a producer of essential food staples, affordability remains at the centre of our decision-making. At a time when inflationary pressures, energy costs, foreign exchange volatility, and global supply-chain disruptions continue to challenge businesses and households alike, we have remained focused on improving efficiency across our operations. This means optimising procurement, strengthening local sourcing, diversifying our energy mix, investing in operational excellence, and building greater supply-chain resilience. By doing so, we are better positioned to absorb some cost pressures internally before they reach consumers. That balance matters. A food manufacturer must be profitable enough to sustain investment and growth, but it must also recognise the critical role its products play in the daily lives of millions of families. Sustainable food security therefore depends on achieving both commercial viability and consumer accessibility. By responding to the practical needs of bakers and recognising that baking is both a craft and a business, we aim to support the people whose work feeds communities and sustains livelihoods. When bakers can make informed product choices and build their businesses, the benefits extend beyond the bakery to distributors, retailers, employees, and families. From manufacturing capacity to economic capacity The impact of food manufacturing extends well beyond the products on market shelves. When indigenous companies invest in large-scale industrial capacity, they create value across entire economic ecosystems. Jobs are created. Technical skills are developed. Local suppliers are strengthened. Logistics networks expand. More economic value is retained within the country. This is why our growth strategy is not simply about becoming bigger. It is about becoming more impactful. As our Chairman, Alhaji Abdul Samad Rabiu, CON, CFR, has consistently emphasised, Nigeria needs strong indigenous enterprises capable of competing at the highest level, investing for the long term, and creating enduring value for society. Our ambition is to be one of those companies. We aspire to be a leading African food manufacturing champion, capable of serving domestic demand while competing successfully across other markets. Indeed, Nigeria cannot fully realise its economic potential without building companies that can produce at scale, drive industrialisation, and compete globally. Through our integrated manufacturing platform and continuing investments, BUA Foods is positioning itself to play an even greater role in strengthening food production, food availability, and economic development across Nigeria and Africa. Nourishing tomorrow requires investment today There is no single solution to food insecurity. It requires stronger agricultural productivity, improved infrastructure, efficient logistics, enhanced storage facilities, access to finance, local sourcing, supportive policies, and critically, large-scale food processing capacity. For BUA Foods, our responsibility is clear. We will continue investing in capacity, technology, operational excellence, people, and local value chains because these are the foundations upon which long-term food security is built. Our first-half performance in 2026 reinforces this strategy. Despite a challenging operating environment, we delivered ₦292.27 billion in profit after tax, representing 12% growth, while gross profit margin improved to 47.5%. These results strengthen our confidence to continue investing for the future. Ultimately, the future belongs to organisations willing to think beyond the next quarter and invest in the next generation. At BUA Foods, that is exactly what we are doing. For us, “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow.” is more than a theme. It is a philosophy that reflects our responsibility as one of Nigeria’s leading food manufacturing companies. We will continue to expand capacity, improve efficiency, strengthen local supply chains, introduce products that respond to evolving consumer needs, and invest in the infrastructure required to build a more resilient food system. Because when we strengthen food production, we strengthen households. When we strengthen manufacturing, we strengthen economies. And when we invest today in the capacity to nourish people, we create a stronger, more secure, and more prosperous future for Nigeria and Africa. That is what Nourishing Lives means to us. About the author: Engr. Ayodele Musibau Abioye, PhD, MNSE, is the Managing Director of BUA Foods Plc and a distinguished business leader and engineer with over 30 years of experience in business and manufacturing engineering. He has expertise spanning operations, manufacturing, supply chain management and business development. He joined BUA Group in 2021 as Chief Operating Officer, overseeing its food businesses, and was subsequently appointed Managing Director of BUA Foods Plc. He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Ilorin, a Master’s degree in Engineering Management and a PhD in Manufacturing Engineering from the University of Benin. He is a registered engineer with the Nigerian Society of Engineers and the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria.
